Join us as we celebrate Homecoming the best way we know how: with great food, cold drinks, and even better company! We'll be serving the Georgia Tech community before and during the Homecoming football game, so whether you're a student, alum, faculty member, there's a spot for you at our table.

value.name: Murph Madness
value.description:
Come test your limits by doing a Murph with Calisthenics Club!

This is a FREE event open to all students!

What is a Murph? A Murph is a fitness challenge created in memory of Navy Seal Lt. Michael Murphy.


We have also created a Mini Murph option for less experienced athletes!

The full muprh:

- 1 mile run

- 100 pullups

- 200 pushups

- 300 squats

- and another mile. 


The Mini Murph:


- 2/3 mile run

- 100 rows

- 200 knee pushups

- 300 squats

- another 2/3 mile

value.name: Socialist Book Club!
value.description:
Join the Young Democratic Socialists of America for our Fall 2026 Book Club! We will be reading If We Burn: The Mass Protest Decade and the Missing Revolution. Below is a synopsis of the book.

Our discussion sessions will be every other Sunday at 10:00 am hybrid in the Georgia Tech library and on Zoom. Check this document for more information. Please register for the Zoom to join.

"From 2010 to 2020, more people participated in protests than at any other point in human history. Yet we are not living in more just and democratic societies as a result. Acclaimed journalist Vincent Bevins carried out hundreds of interviews around the world, guided by a single, puzzling question: How did so many mass protests lead to the opposite of what they asked for?

The result is a stirring work of history that connects events in a dozen countries and reveals that conventional wisdom on revolutionary change is gravely misguided. From the so-called Arab Spring to Gezi Park in Turkey, from Ukraine’s Euromaidan to student rebellions in Chile and Hong Kong, Bevins provides a blow-by-blow account of street movements and their consequences, recounted in gripping detail.

In this groundbreaking study of an extraordinary chain of events, protesters and major actors look back on successes and defeats, offering urgent lessons for the future."

value.name: Workshop #1: Intro to GPU/CUDA Programming
value.description: This is the first workshop in our Supercomputing Club’s workshop series, introducing students to GPU programming and NVIDIA CUDA. We will cover the basics of GPUs and CUDA, followed by hands-on examples that demonstrate how GPUs can accelerate computations. The workshop will progress from a simple vector sum to different techniques for improving performance, including parallel reductions and shared memory. Students will also have the opportunity to access Georgia Tech’s PACE ICE environment and try out CUDA programming themselves. This workshop aims to introduce students to GPU programming and establish a foundation for future workshops on high-performance and parallel computing. ALL STUDENTS ARE WELCOME.

value.name: Campus Outreach Monday Night Meeting
value.description: CO Weekly meetings are designed to be a safe space to invite college students from all areas of our staff’s influence with the aim to clearly present the Gospel and express God’s love in a way that is life-transformational. In an effort to be fun and relevant while also seeking to display the aspects of a Christ-centered ministry, we will prioritize the Word, model a prayerful dependence on God, enhance the community-feel of our meeting with discussion questions, games, and refreshments, and lastly, maximize our opportunities for co-ed fellowship among our students at the beginning of the meeting.

value.name: Graduate Internship Program College Level Data Sharing (College of Design)(Virtual)

Together, we’ll explore what the data tells us, identify opportunities for greater collaboration and student support, and discuss how we can continue connecting graduate students with meaningful internship experiences.
